title: High-Protein Crispy Peanut Tofu and Edamame Stir-Fry
description: Crispy golden tofu cubes and tender edamame stir-fried with fresh vegetables in a savory garlic-ginger peanut sauce. Packed with 26g of plant-based protein per serving.

ingredients.note: such as avocado or canola oil, divided

steps: In a medium bowl, toss the cubed extra-firm tofu with cornstarch until every cube is lightly and evenly coated. Heat 1 tablespoon of neutral cooking oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet or wok over medium-high heat for 2 minutes until shimmering.

Add the coated tofu cubes to the hot skillet in a single layer. Cook over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until all sides are deep golden brown and crisp. Transfer the tofu to a plate and set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together the creamy peanut butter, low-sodium soy sauce, maple syrup, lime juice, minced garlic, grated ginger, and warm water until completely smooth and pourable.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of neutral cooking oil to the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add the broccoli florets and sliced red bell pepper; stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a lid, and steam for 2 minutes until the broccoli is tender-crisp and bright green.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the thawed edamame, crispy cooked tofu, and prepared peanut sauce into the skillet. Stir continuously for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is evenly coated, warmed through, and the sauce bubbles slightly. Remove from heat and serve hot.
tips: Press the tofu with a tofu press or heavy pan wrapped in paper towels for at least 15 minutes before cubing to remove excess water for maximum crispiness.
Swap edamame or broccoli for snap peas or baby spinach if adjusting veggies to your macro needs.
Store sauce separately if prepping ingredients ahead of time to keep tofu ultra-crispy upon reheating.
storage: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes to regain crispness.

steps_short: Toss pressed tofu cubes in cornstarch until lightly coated.
Pan-fry in sesame oil for 8 minutes until golden and crispy.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime, garlic, and ginger until smooth.
Stir-fry broccoli, red peppers, and edamame for 4 minutes.
Toss everything in the peanut sauce until hot and coated.

issues: Using sesame oil as the high-heat cooking oil for 8-10 minutes of pan-frying tofu will cause the oil to smoke and turn bitter due to its low smoke point. A high-smoke-point neutral oil (such as canola or avocado oil) should be used for cooking instead.

Stir-frying raw broccoli florets for 3-4 minutes without adding liquid or steaming will leave them tough and undercooked. Adding 2 tablespoons of water and covering the pan briefly is required to properly steam the broccoli until tender-crisp.
